Appellant company M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. has filed this appeal challenging the M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 1 of 8 impugned order passed by the Adjudicating Officer on 25.11.2016 whereby the Adjudicating Officer imposed a penalty of Rs.10,000/ on Sh.Sajjan Singh, Rs.40,000/ on M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetables Pvt. sentences.text: 2. The brief facts of the case are that the appellant company is engaged in manufacturing and sale of milk and milk products in various states of Delhi.

The Food Safety Officer of Govt. of Delhi under The Food Safety & Standards Act 2006(FSS Act in short) took the sample of Full Cream Milk and on analysis at Delhi Govt. Lab, it was reported to be Substandard by Food Analyst Delhi which is as follows:
Marketing Unit And Regd.Office At vs Shri Hukam Singh on 7 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98117479/
1 a.)Milk Fat was found to be 6.1% as against standard of FCM of 6.0%;
b.)Solids Non Fat(SNF) was found to be 8.64% as against 9%.
Thus, milk was reported to be marginally deficient in SNF to the extent of only 0.36%
whereas fat was even above the prescribed M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 2 of 8 limit of 6.0%.
3.

entities.text: Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 2 of 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant has challenged the order of the Adjudicating Officer on the ground that there was only marginal deficiency in the sample of Full Cream Milk which could be due to human error while analyzing the sample and therefore, in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Narottam Dass Vs. State of Rajasthan, 1995(1) FAC 126, the Adjudicating Officer should have dismissed the report of the Food Analyst.

entities.text: Narottam Dass Vs. State of Rajasthan, 1995(1) FAC 126
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant has further submitted that the Adjudicating Officer also failed to consider the law laid down in Nagar Swasthya Adhikari Vs. Subhash Chandra and Others, 1982(1) FAC 97 wherein it was interalia held that if the SNF is deficient in the sample of milk then it can only be concluded that either the sample taken was not proper or analysis has not been done properly.

entities.text: Nagar Swasthya Adhikari Vs. Subhash Chandra and Others, 1982(1) FAC 97
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant has further submitted that the Food Safety Officer has not adopted the correct measure while taking the sample and this was not taken into account by the Adjudicating Officer.

The Food Analyst also in violation of Section 42(2) of FSS Act did not mention the method of taking of sample immediately before taking of sample for analysis and therefore, in the absence of the same, the report of the Food Analyst is illegal.

The appellant has also taken the plea that the M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 3 of 8 lab where the sample was analyzed was neither NABL accredited nor the same was notified by Food Authority as per Section 43 of FSS Act.

entities.text: M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has further been submitted that by the virtue of an advisory issued u/S 98 of FSS Act is not sufficient to change the status of lab or make the lab valid.
The appellant has submitted that the Adjudicating Officer has wrongly imposed penalty twice upon it for manufacturing and selling milk.
It has further been submitted that the Adjudicating Officer did not appreciate the defense of due diligence being put forward by the appellant.

4. The perusal of the order of the Adjudicating Officer indicates that he had rejected the plea of the appellant that the sample was not properly stirred/homogenized on the ground that no proper documentary evidence was proved that proper procedure/method was not followed by the Food Analyst.
The Adjudicating Officer noted that the Food Analyst stated in his cross examination that every method prescribed in DGHS manual was duly followed.
The defense of the marginal variations was also rejected by the Adjudicating Officer in view of the health of general public and future generations of the country.
5. Ld.

Counsel for the appellant has submitted that since there is a marginal variation and the appellant has a reputation of having very good infrastructure and robust mechanism for M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd.

sentences.text: Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 4 of 8 manufacturing milk in hygienic conditions, the Adjudicating Officer should not have imposed the penalty upon the appellant.
It has further been submitted that the order of the Adjudicating Officer imposing penalty twice upon the appellant is also beyond the realm of the law.

sentences.text:
Per contra, Ld.Chief PP for the respondent has submitted that all the contentions of the appellant are liable to be rejected in view of the latest judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2019) 9 SCC 427.
7.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh, (2019) 9 SCC 427
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions of the parties and perused the record carefully.

8. In M.V.Joshi Vs. M.U.Shimpi, AIR 1961 SC 1494, it was interalia held as under:
"7....Therefore, if the quality or purity of butter falls below the standard prescribed by the said rule or its constituents are in excess of the prescribed limits of variability, it shall be deemed to be adulterated within the meaning of Section 2 of the Act.
If the prescribed standard is not attained, the statute treats such butter, by fiction, as an adulterated food, though in fact it is not adulterated.

To put it in other words, by reason of the fiction, it is not permissible for an accused to prove M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 5 of 8 that, though the standard prescribed is not attained, the article of food is in fact not adulterated.

entities.text: M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The non conformity with the standard prescribed makes such butter an adulterated food.
Section 7 of the Act prohibits the manufacture, sale, storage or distribution of such food."

9. Similarly, in State of Kerala Vs. Parameswaram Pillai Vasudevan Nair, 1975 Cri LJ 97, it was interalia held as under:
"14.The

entities.text: State of Kerala Vs. Parameswaram Pillai Vasudevan Nair, 1975 Cri LJ 97
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Act is a piece of consumer legislation.
It regulates to some extent the consumersupplier relations.
Consumerists demand enforcement of discipline among the producers or manufacturers of food to ensure safety in the realm of food.
The consumer's legitimate ignorance and his almost total dependence on the fairness and competence of those who supply his daily needs have made him a ready target for exploitation.
The Act is intended to protect him against outright frauds.
15. The Act does not make a distinction between cases coming under it on the basis of the degree of adulteration.
It does not provide for aggravation of offence based on the extent of contamination.
The offence and punishment are the same whether the adulteration is great or small.

Food pollution, even if it be only to the slightest extent,
if continued in practice, would adversely affect the health of every man, woman and child in the country.

Hence even marginal or border line variations of the prescribed standards under the Act are matters of serious concern for all and as public interests are involved in them, the maxim, de minimis non curat lex law does not concern itself about trifles, does not apply to them.
16. The standard fixed under the Act is one that is certain.

If it is varied to any extent the certainty of a M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Marketing Unit And Regd.Office At vs Shri Hukam Singh on 7 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98117479/
3

entities.text: M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Marketing Unit And Regd.Office At vs Shri Hukam Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Officer Page No. 6 of 8 general standard would be replaced by the vagaries of a fluctuating standard.
The disadvantages of the resulting unpredictability, uncertainty and impossibility of arriving at fair and consistent decisions, are great.
17. The Act does not provide for exemption of marginal or border line variations of the standard from the operation of the Act.
In such circumstances to condone such variations on the ground that they are negligible is virtually to alter the standard itself fixed under the Act.
18. The standards of qualities of the articles have been fixed by the Government under the provisions of the Act after due deliberation and after consulting a committee of competent men.
It is for them to give due allowance for probable errors before fixing a standard.
They may have done it also.
There is no reason to assume otherwise.

Therefore the conclusion is that for an article of food when a standard has been fixed under the Act it has to be observed in every detail."
10.

Hon'ble Supreme Court after taking into account all the judgments on this issue in Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh's case (Supra) interalia held as under: "7.We are of the considered view that once standards are laid down by the legislature then those standards have to be followed.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In items like milk which is a primary food, under the Act, it is not necessary to also prove that the food item had become unfit for human consumption or injurious to health.
In cases of food coming under the Act, it is not required to prove that article of food was injurious to health.
In this case, the only question to be determined is whether the article complies with the standards laid down or not?
If it fails to comply with the standards then it will have to be treated as an adulterated article even if it is not rendered injurious to health.
Even marginal deviation from the M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer Page No. 7 of 8 prescribed standard cannot be ignored."

entities.text: M/s Mother Dairy Fruit and Vegetable Pvt. Ltd. Vs Food Safety Officer
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. I consider that in Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh's case (Supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has made the law very clear on this point and now, it is a settled proposition that if the standards are not complied with, the appellant cannot be let off only on the ground that the variation is marginal.

entities.text: Raj Kumar Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I do not see any illegality in the impugned order dated 25.11.2016 passed by the Adjudicating Officer.
There is also no force in other contentions raised by the appellant in appeal, furthermore, the same have also not been pressed during the course of submissions.

Hence,
the appeal is dismissed.
12. Trial Court record be sent back alongwith copy of this judgment.
13. Appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
Announced in open court (DINESH KUMAR SHARMA) on 07.02.2020.
